method: Machine-learned crop suitability (model crop-suitability-v3.1): one XGBoost model per crop, trained on where 40 crops are grown today (IFPRI MapSPAM 2020, 22,450 farmland cells worldwide), each cell described by 10 climate features from six NASA POWER measurements, 2001 to 2025. On regions held out of training it tells places that grow a crop from places that do not with AUC 0.90. Rain only also needs enough rain: scores fade to 0 below 100 mm a year (200 mm is full strength for wheat and barley, 250 mm for other crops). Future years: the four temperature features' own 2001 to 2025 trends (Theil-Sen) continued, with a 95% range from 200 resamples of the years; rain, humidity and soil wetness are held at their 2001 to 2025 average, because their NASA records break around 2015 over Egypt. Not a forecast.
source: NASA POWER climate and a model trained on IFPRI MapSPAM 2020 crop maps
score_note: A score runs from 0 to 100: how typical this climate is of the places where the crop is grown today. 50 means as typical of places that grow it as of places that do not. It is not a yield and not the chance of a good harvest. Irrigated assumes water can be supplied; it does not show that water exists here. Rain, humidity and soil wetness are their 2001 to 2025 averages, because their NASA records break around 2015 over Egypt; changes to 2030 and 2035 come from the measured warming only. Crops Egypt grows only on small areas (soybean, sunflower, chickpea, lentil) can score low even where they are grown. Olive and date palm are not separate crops in the crop maps and are not covered.
